t.5.5.2: Then the glorious one reached the dwelling of the lord of the Rākṣasas, which was encircled by a shining rampart having the colour of the sun.
t.5.5.1: That monkey, able to assume any form at will, moving freely along its winding ways, roamed through Laṅkā, endowed with lightness and agility.
t.5.5.3: Gazing upon the mansion, guarded by fearsome rākṣasas as a great forest is guarded by lions, the elephant among monkeys shone forth.
t.5.5.4: It was surrounded by bright archways inlaid with silver and adorned with gold, by wonderfully varied courtyards, and by beautiful gateways.
t.5.5.5: It was attended by elephant-keepers mounted on elephants, by tireless heroes, and by irresistible horses that drew the chariots.
t.5.5.6: It was ever traversed by rumbling, many-hued chariots fitted with protective coverings of lion and tiger skins and adorned with ivory, gold and silver.
t.5.5.7: It was strewn with many jewels and furnished with costly seats and vessels, the dwelling of great chariot-warriors, filled with great chariots and grand seats.
t.5.5.8: It was filled on every side with lovely and most magnificent sights, and with all those birds and beasts of many kinds, in their many thousands.
t.5.5.9: It was well guarded by disciplined frontier-wardens and by rākṣasas, and it was filled on every side with eminent and excellent women.
t.5.5.10: He beheld the dwelling of the lord of the rākṣasas, graced with jewels of joyful women, and resounding like the roar of the ocean with the jingling of their splendid ornaments.
t.5.5.11: That palace was endowed with royal excellences and with the finest choice sandalwoods, resounding with the sound of kettledrums and mṛdaṅga drums, and echoing with the blare of conches.
t.5.5.12: Constantly worshipped, receiving oblations on the festival days, and always honoured by the rākṣasas, it was like the deep ocean, like the resounding ocean.
t.5.5.13: That great monkey beheld the great mansion of the mighty one, furnished with splendid jewels and thronged with a great multitude of people.
t.5.5.14: Resplendent in its form and thronged with elephants, horses and chariots, it was, the great monkey thought, the very ornament of Laṅkā.
t.5.5.15: Fearless indeed, that monkey moved from house to house of the Rākṣasas, gazing upon their gardens and their palaces as he went.
t.5.5.16: Having leapt down upon the dwelling of Prahasta, the mighty one of great speed then sprang to another abode, that of Mahāpārśva.
t.5.5.17: Then that great monkey leapt onto the dwelling of Kumbhakarṇa, which resembled a cloud, and likewise onto that of Vibhīṣaṇa.
t.5.5.18: That great monkey likewise leapt onto the mansion of Mahodara, and of Virūpākṣa too, of Vidyujjihva and likewise of Vidyunmālin, and also of Vajradaṃṣṭra.
t.5.5.19: The swift leader of the monkey troops went to the dwelling of Śuka, and of the wise Sāraṇa, and likewise of Indrajit.
t.5.5.20: The leader of the monkey troops went to the dwelling of Jambumālin and of Sumāli, of Raśmiketu, and likewise of Sūryaśatru.
t.5.5.21: The son of Māruta came to the mansion of Dhūmrākṣa and of Sampāti, and to those of Vidyudrūpa, Bhīma, Ghana and Vighana.
t.5.5.22: Of Śukanābha, Vakra, Śaṭha and Vikaṭa, of Hrasvakarṇa and Daṃṣṭra, and of the rākṣasa Romaśa.
t.5.5.23: Of Yuddhonmatta, of Matta, of Dhvajagrīva, of Nādin, of Vidyujjihva and Indrajihva, and likewise of Hastimukha.
t.5.5.25: In each of those very costly mansions, that great monkey of great renown beheld the opulence of those opulent ones.
t.5.5.24: Hanumān, the son of Māruta, moving on step by step, went to the abodes of Karāla, of Piśāca, and indeed of Śoṇitākṣa.
t.5.5.26: Having passed beyond the dwellings of all of them on every side, the glorious one then reached the residence of the lord of the Rākṣasas.
t.5.5.27: As he roamed about, that best of monkeys, a tiger among monkeys, saw the rākṣasīs who lay sleeping near Rāvaṇa, women with hideous eyes, holding spears and clubs in their hands and bearing lances and javelins.
t.5.5.28: In the house of that lord of the rākṣasas, he saw various companies of guards.
t.5.5.29: He saw red, white, pale and tawny ones of great swiftness, and well-bred, handsome elephants that crush the elephants of the enemy.
t.5.5.30: In that house he saw, stationed in the elephant quarters, beasts equal to Airāvata in battle, slayers of enemy armies.
t.5.5.31: He saw them, dripping like clouds pouring rain and streaming like mountains running with torrents, roaring with the rumble of thundering clouds, unassailable by enemies in battle.
t.5.5.32: There he saw a thousand troops adorned with jāmbūnada gold, covered without a break in nets of gold and shining like the newly risen sun.
t.5.5.33: In the residence of Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, that monkey, the son of Māruta, saw palanquins of various shapes.
t.5.5.34: He saw wondrous bowers of creepers and picture-galleries, other pleasure-houses too, and even artificial hills made of wood.
t.5.5.35: In the residence of Rāvaṇa, lord of the Rākṣasas, he saw a charming chamber of love and also a chamber for daytime use.
t.5.5.36: He saw that finest of mansions, resembling the slopes of Mount Mandara, crowded with the haunts of peacocks and strewn with flagstaffs.
t.5.5.38: And then, by the flames of its jewels and by the splendour of Rāvaṇa, that mansion blazed forth like the rayed sun with its rays.
t.5.5.37: The mansion had endless heaps of jewels and a wealth of treasures on every side, and its works had been finished by skilled craftsmen, like the dwelling of Bhūtapati.
t.5.5.39: The leader of the monkey troops saw couches and seats made entirely of Jāmbūnada gold, and gleaming vessels as well.
t.5.5.40: Moist with spilled honey-wine and crowded with jewelled vessels, the palace was delightful and spacious, like the mansion of Kubera.
t.5.5.41: The place was made to resound with the jingling of anklets, the tinkling of girdles, and the loud, resonant sounds of mṛdaṅga drums and clapping palms.
t.5.5.42: Hanumān entered the great mansion, which was joined to clusters of palaces, crowded with hundreds of jewel-like women, and laid out with well-arranged courtyards.
